expectations.text: Applies the honesty check: publishes only criteria that will actually be applied, acknowledging name recognition and topic mix will shape selection
expectations.evidence: Section 2 says: 'Publish only criteria you will really apply. The skill's honesty check applies: name recognition and topic mix do shape selection.' The brief also makes criteria 1 and 6 conditional on real practice, so it does not promise what it won't apply. However, the draft criteria text that would be published never says that name recognition or topic mix shape selection. Only criterion 3, on local and out-of-town balance, partly touches topic mix. The brief states the honesty check but does not carry it into the published text.

expectations.text: Applies the honesty check: publishes only criteria that will actually be applied, acknowledging name recognition and topic mix will shape selection
expectations.evidence: The transcript recommends publishing criteria and weights. Its example rubric has 'Fit with themes' and 'Speaker's ability to deliver (past talks, video...)', and section 1 says to unblind 'to check for pitches and to balance the program.' These hint at topic mix and speaker track record. The transcript never says to publish only the criteria that will really be applied. It never admits that name recognition and draw will shape selection. It also never says the published rubric should state that topic and program balance can override scores. Instead it presents the published rubric plus blind
